title: Yorkshire Pudding
subtitle: Classic risen batter pudding, crisp outside and hollow within
excerpt: Light, hollow, dramatically risen batter puddings made from eggs, flour, and milk, baked in a blistering hot tin until they tower above the rim. The essential companion to roast beef.

recipe.sourceNotes: Yorkshire pudding is a baked batter dish originating in Yorkshire in the north of England, where it has been served since at least the eighteenth century. The first recorded recipe appears in 1737 in a book called The Whole Duty of a Woman. Historically the pudding was served as a first course before the main meal of roast beef, with gravy, to take the edge off the appetite before the expensive meat arrived. The modern convention of serving it alongside the roast as a side dish is a later development. The batter is identical to that used for pancakes and toad in the hole: eggs, flour, and milk in roughly equal proportions by weight. The Yorkshire Pudding must meet several criteria to be considered correct: it must rise above the height of the tin, it must be hollow inside, and its sides must be crisp. The keys are: hot fat, rested batter, a very hot oven, and no opening the door during baking.

recipeTools.notes: A 12-hole muffin tin or a 4-hole Yorkshire pudding tin.

content.text: The fat in the tin holes must be smoking before the batter goes in: this is non-negotiable. Use a fat with a high smoke point: beef dripping (the most traditional), lard, or vegetable oil. Pour the batter quickly and return the tin to the oven fast. Do not open the door for the first 20 minutes. Resting the batter for at least 30 minutes, and up to several hours in the fridge, improves the rise and the texture of the finished puddings.

items.preparation: or beef dripping; for the tin

content.text: Sift the flour and salt into a large bowl. Make a well and add the eggs. Whisk together, then gradually whisk in the milk to a smooth batter. Rest for at least 30 minutes, or overnight in the fridge.
Heat the oven to 230 C / fan 210 C / gas 8. Put a teaspoon of oil into each hole of a 12-hole muffin tin (or the 4-hole pudding tin). Heat in the oven for 5 to 8 minutes until the oil is smoking.

Working quickly, pour the batter into each hole until two-thirds full. Return to the oven immediately. Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until tall, crisp, and golden-brown. Do not open the oven for the first 20 minutes. Serve at once.
